body:
Look at any vape, e-liquid or pouch sold in the United States and you will find a warning: "WARNING: This product contains nicotine. Nicotine is an addictive chemical." It is short, it appears on every package, and it is easy to skim past. This guide explains what the warning is, why it exists, what it tells you, where to find it, what it does not say, what other warnings you may see and why we repeat it throughout our site. It is general information, not legal advice or medical advice. Laws change and differ by state and city, so check the rules where you live. Everything we sell is for adults aged 21 and over, and nicotine is addictive.

## Why the warning exists
The FDA requires the warning on the packaging and in advertisements for nicotine products. It must be clear, prominent and in a set format. It exists to remind adults that nicotine is addictive, and it applies whatever the brand, the flavor or the type of device. When you see it, it is a reminder that these products carry a real risk of dependence, and that they are intended only for adults.

## What it tells you
Nicotine is a stimulant that the body can become dependent on. Using a product that contains it can lead to cravings and dependence, which is why products are limited to adults aged 21 and over. The word "addictive" is not a figure of speech: it means that regular use can make it hard to stop, and that stopping may cause withdrawal symptoms. The warning does not tell you how addictive a particular product is, or compare it with other products. It tells you that the substance is addictive.

### What dependence can feel like
People describe dependence as strong cravings, irritability, difficulty concentrating, restlessness or a feeling that they need a product to feel normal. These experiences differ from person to person. If you recognize them, or if you worry about your use, speak to a healthcare professional. We cannot give medical advice, and nothing here is medical advice.

## Where to find it
On the front or side panel of the package, often in a bordered box, and in advertisements and on websites that sell the product. On a disposable, it is on the box and often on the device. On a bottle, it is on the label. On a can of pouches, it is on the lid or side. You will also see it on our site, at the age gate, in the announcement bar and on product pages. If a product has no warning, treat it with caution and do not buy it. A missing or reworded warning can be a sign that the product does not meet the rules, or that it is not genuine. See [how to spot counterfeit vapes](/blog/how-to-spot-counterfeit-vapes/).

## What it does not say
It does not describe a product as more or less harmful than any other. It makes no comparison between nicotine products and anything else. We do not make health comparisons, and neither should sellers. If a seller makes claims about health benefits or about being less risky, be cautious, because such claims are tightly regulated. See [the FDA and vaping products](/blog/fda-and-vaping-products-what-adults-should-know/).

## Other warnings you may see
You may see notes for pregnant or nursing women, for people with health conditions and for children and pets. Follow them. Typical statements include that products are not for use by anyone under 21, that they should be kept out of reach of children and pets and that anyone with a medical condition or taking medication should ask a professional before use. These are separate from the nicotine warning, and they come from the manufacturer or from local rules. Nothing here is medical advice; consult a healthcare professional with questions.

### State and local warnings
Some states require additional notices, such as signs in shops or specific statements on products. If you live in such a state, you may see more text than the federal statement. These do not replace the federal warning; they add to it.

## How we use the warning
We show the warning where it matters: at our age gate, in our site banner, on product pages and in our policies. We do so because it is required, and because it is the right thing to do. Repeating it is not a formality. It is a reminder that every product on this site contains nicotine, is for adults only and carries a risk of dependence. Read our [FDA disclaimer](/fda-disclaimer/) and [terms](/terms/) for more.

## Reading the label as a whole
The warning is one part of a label. A good habit is to read the whole label before you use a product: the strength, the volume, the ingredients where listed, the manufacturer's details, the instructions and the warnings. If any of these is missing or looks wrong, ask us before you use it. See [how to read an e-liquid label](/blog/how-to-read-an-e-liquid-label/) and [nicotine strength guide](/blog/nicotine-strength-guide/).

## Common questions
### Does the warning apply to nicotine pouches?
Yes. Products that contain nicotine carry the warning, including pouches, liquids and devices.

### Does a zero-nicotine product need the warning?
Products labelled as containing no nicotine may carry different notices. Check the label. We label zero-nicotine products clearly on the product page.

### Why is the warning so blunt?
Because it is meant to be clear. A direct statement is easier to understand and harder to ignore than a long explanation.

### Can a seller remove or hide it?
No. Removing or hiding the warning is against the rules. If a product arrives without one, contact us.

### Does the warning mean I should not use the product?
It means you should understand the risk before you use it. These products are for adults who choose to use nicotine, and anyone with concerns should speak to a healthcare professional.

## Related
See the [FDA overview](/blog/fda-and-vaping-products-what-adults-should-know/) and our [FDA disclaimer](/fda-disclaimer/). Learn about [nicotine strength](/blog/nicotine-strength-guide/). Browse [disposable vapes](/shop/disposables/). All products are for adults aged 21 and over, and nicotine is addictive.

## Why the wording is so plain
The warning is written in simple words so that anyone can understand it at a glance, in the seconds a person spends looking at a package. It states two facts: the product contains nicotine, and nicotine is addictive. It does not hedge, and it does not tell a story. That directness is the point. If you remember only one thing from a label, it should be this.

## A worked example: reading a bottle
You pick up a bottle of e-liquid. On the front, you see the brand and the flavor. On the side, in a box, you see the warning. On the back, you see the strength, the volume, the ratio and the manufacturer's details. You read the warning, check that the strength is what you intended and look at the volume. You now know what you are buying, and that it is for adults only. If any part of the label were missing, you would ask the seller before using the product.

## Talking about the warning with others
If someone you know uses nicotine products, the warning is a neutral starting point for a conversation, not an accusation. It says the same thing to everyone: nicotine is addictive. If a friend or relative wants to cut down or stop, they can speak to a healthcare professional about the support that is available. If you are a parent, the warning is a good reason to keep products locked away and to talk to older children about why they are for adults only.

## Frequently asked questions in depth
### Does the warning change with strength?
The statement is the same regardless of strength. The strength is shown separately on the label, and our [nicotine strength guide](/blog/nicotine-strength-guide/) explains how to read it.

### Who enforces the warning rule?
Federal regulators enforce labeling requirements, and sellers that ignore them can face action. As a buyer, your role is to read the label and to be cautious of products without one.

### Do ads need the warning too?
Yes. Advertisements for nicotine products must carry the statement, which is why you see it on product pages and in our site banner.

### Can the warning be in another language?
The required statement must be in English on products for the U.S. market. Packaging only in another language is a concern, because it may not have been made for this market.

## Using the warning as a check on products
The warning can also serve as a quick quality check. When you receive a product, look for the statement in the right place, in clear English, in the right words. If it is missing, faded, misspelled or different from the standard wording, ask the seller. Properly labelled products are a sign that the maker and the seller follow the rules, and unlabelled ones are a sign that something may be wrong. Take the extra few seconds on every new product.

## Why we mention it so often
You will see the statement on our age gate, in our banner and across our site. That repetition is deliberate. We would rather remind you too often than too rarely, because the message is simple and important: these products contain nicotine, nicotine is addictive and they are for adults aged 21 and over.
